summary: This is a reference page for the H3_POINT_TO_CELL_STRING function, which returns the hexadecimal H3 cell ID for a GEOGRAPHY Point at a given resolution. It gives the syntax, the two arguments (a geography point and an integer resolution from 0 to 15), and the VARCHAR return value. Two examples are shown: a valid call for the Brandenburg Gate at resolution 8, and an invalid call at resolution 18 that produces an error.
one_line: Reference for the H3_POINT_TO_CELL_STRING function, which returns the hexadecimal H3 cell ID of a geography point at a chosen resolution.
key_facts: H3_POINT_TO_CELL_STRING returns the hexadecimal H3 cell ID for a given location and resolution.
The function takes a GEOGRAPHY object representing a Point as its first argument.
The second argument, target_resolution, must be an INTEGER between 0 and 15 inclusive.
Specifying any target_resolution value other than 0 through 15 results in an error.
The function returns a VARCHAR value.
The example returns the hexadecimal H3 cell ID for the Brandenburg Gate at resolution 8.
The Brandenburg Gate example uses ST_POINT(13.377704, 52.516262) as the point.
The resolution 8 example returns the cell ID 881F1D4887FFFFF.
The example with resolution 18 fails with error 100410 (P0000): Invalid H3 resolution value: 18.
The error message states that resolution must be between 0 (coarsest) and 15 (finest).
The page is listed under the H3 category of the function catalog, within the Conversion, Output, Formatting group context shown in navigation.
